items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: my piano player was John Malachi. ... I picked up another band in Washington ... was Harry Curtis ... John Malachi, Tommy Potter and Leo Williamson.

ctx.x: I don't know. I'd have to go back and find that year when it was. But I had a little band at the Yacht Club on 52nd Street, and my piano player was John Malachi. My bass player was Tommy Potter. I got them out of Washington. And they went with Billy Eckstine later on, the
two of them with Billy Eckstine's big band. But I can't -- I couldn't tell you the year. I really couldn't tell you.

items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: Trummy, after having met me in Tommy Miles' band... When he left Jimmy Lunceford, he came down to see me... He told me about this idea that he had about getting this little band together.

ctx.x: I think it was Buddy Johnson and Les Hite and Billy Eckstine. They played in this huge tobacco warehouse, and they had three big bands there. But in Washington, after this dance, we were wondering "What we gonna do?" you know. You know, we have no drummer. So I told them about this drummer that I knew that was playing at the Crystal Caverns, when I was up with Trummy, and he was a an excellent drummer and a very good reader -- just a good drummer all the way around. His name was... Everybody called him Charlie…
